target_customer: Brands and developers who want to link physical products to the internet or authenticate them; later fashion brands against counterfeiting
problem: Connecting products to the internet or proving authenticity usually needs NFC chips or QR codes; Arylla claimed a printable invisible tag 10x cheaper than NFC.
business_model: API licensing plus ink and printing partnerships
product_category: Invisible ink tags for product authentication and IoT

founders.name: Perry Everett
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page without background.

founders.name: Benjamin Rasera
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page without background.

founders.name: Graham Thomas
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page without background.

exit.reason: YC marks the company Inactive but arylla.com still markets the product and invites demo calls; no shutdown found.

technical_complexity.rationale: The company developed nanotechnology-based ink readable by ordinary smartphones, which meant materials science plus computer vision, built by Waterloo nanotechnology engineers.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary ink chemistry and printing partnerships are hard to replicate, though adoption depends on printers and brands switching from existing authentication methods.

market_need_then: Counterfeiting and traceability were real brand concerns; the YC page pitched the tag as 10x cheaper than NFC, but no customer or revenue figures were found.

branding.domain_note: arylla.com is still live in the fetch and promotes invisible ink for fashion products.
branding.community_and_virality: A CBC piece and a mr-mag feature covered the technology; no evidence of consumer community.

brand_strength.rationale: Some local press coverage of the technology exists, but the name is invented and unexplained and no community or merch signals were found.

pivots.from: Printable chip-less tags licensed to developers as an API (IoT)
pivots.to: Invisible ink for fashion authentication, traceability and engagement
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from the YC description versus the current website, date unknown

outcome_analysis: Arylla's fate is unclear. YC marks it Inactive, but the company's website remains up and a database shows an incubator round in August 2021. The cause of any decline is not public, so no failure factor is assigned. The product moved from an IoT tag API to fashion authentication, and funding sources show only small amounts.
notes: Funding rests on CB Insights and VCBacked aggregator pages: total about $20K across six rounds, latest incubator round dated 2021-08-19 with Plug and Play; the round amount is unknown and the single-database caveat applies. Founded 2016 per YC versus 2015 per CB Insights, which also says the company was formerly Black Box Technologies. The CBC article could not be fetched (HTTP 403), so founder education beyond the website's statement that engineers from the University of Waterloo founded it is unknown. Competitors: YC names NFC as the alternative but no dated company source near the batch was found, so the list is empty. The pivot is inferred and its date is unknown. The Y Combinator status conflicts with the live website.
